# Surgical

This folder catalogs specific surgical procedures and post-operative interventions tracked within the Danish acute surgery quality assessments. It details the primary distinction between open surgery and minimally invasive laparoscopy, tracking their shifting national prevalence and associated anesthesia practices over multiple reporting periods. Additionally, it defines specific procedural cohorts used for clinical quality indicators, such as non-ischemic ileus operations, alongside standardized definitions for post-operative mobilization.

## Pages

- [[aaben-kirurgi|åben kirurgi]] — Open surgery as a primary benchmarked method in the Acute Surgery Database, tracking regional trends and temporal development.
- [[ileusoperationer-uden-iskaemi-eller-perforation|ileusoperationer uden iskæmi eller perforation]] — The specific patient cohort for Indikator 4y, measuring the proportion of non-ischemic ileus patients operated on within a 24-hour window.
- [[laparoskopi]] — Minimally invasive surgery, analyzed for its growing national prevalence compared to open surgery and its specific epidural anesthesia rates.
- [[laparotomi]] — Open abdominal surgery, tracked for its declining national proportion and its quality target regarding epidural anesthesia administration.
- [[mobilisering]] — The clinical definition and tracking of patient mobilization from a lying to a sitting or standing position post-surgery.
